newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANI shares soar, top turnover list.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANI shares soar, top turnover list.

text.p: Shares in engineering company Australian National Industries Ltd (ANI) topped the turnover list on Friday with 13.48 million shares traded.
Brokers said the trade was dominated by two large parcels of five million and six million shares, pushing the stock to a 1996 high of A$1.23, a gain of five cents on Thursday's closing level.

ANI holds its annual general meeting next Monday with directors divided over the handling of the Holter environmental systems acquisition in the early 1990s which has cost the company more than A$200 million in losses and writedowns.

ANI director Ross Palmer, who is also a major shareholder in the Sydney-based company, has criticised the acquisition of the German-based Holter operation, but faces a motion from fellow director Peter Joseph to be removed from the board.

Palmer, in turn, has proposed that Joseph be removed although numerous press reports said institutions had sided with Joseph. An institutional broker said the two key ANI share parcels were specialled by two brokers, from one seller.
Shaw Stockbroking traded five million shares and ANZ Securities dealt six million, both at 11.28 a.m. (0128 GMT).
"It certainly would have gone to institutions," the broker said.
"The stock has been well bid for a while. But I don't know who the seller would be, 11 million (shares) could be any one of a dozen institutions," he said.
An ANI spokesman said the company was aware of the share trading, but had no information about the transactions.
ANI has 785.87 million shares on issue and is valued at A$974.48 million at current prices.
